Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Registration for exchange students opened the day before the start of classes and are done online. One chooses their desired courses with one of two teams.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I had no issues.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was able to register for all my pre-approved courses. Some other courses were already unavailable or had a low amount of remaining places.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Get up early for registration. You should already know which courses you are registering for, and the process shouldn't take more than a few minutes.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had courses from every year of the bachelor curriculum but generally found them all decently interesting and challenging.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Presence in class is valued much higher. The teachers are generally quite a bit more specialized, with some courses being taught by two or more professors according to their area of expertise.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Turn of the century, Novecentismo and the avantgardes in Spanish literature
Fiction and the novel in the Golden Age
Historic grammar of the Spanish language
The invention of a poetic language in the Golden Age
Spanish and languages of the Hispanic world
Literature (2nd language): Arabic
an additional basic course in Catalan language, offered by the university to all students.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The course Turn of the century, Novecentismo and the avantgardes in Spanish literature is very interesting and taught by a very dedicated professor. Touches upon some areas of literary history that were not as elaborate in the bachelor curriculum at home.

questions.answer: Public transit is quite affordable in Valencia. Everything is generally a great deal cheaper than Copenhagen.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I recommend the city's many art museums, especially IVAM which has a very dense and fascinating collection of modern and contemporary art. The Turia gardens also deserve a special mention; they are accessible from virtually every part of the city.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Took a few weeks, perhaps. The daily rhythm is very different from that of Scandinavia.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Don't worry too much about language.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None that come to mind.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Ubiquity of cafés and other such gathering spots.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Don't undervalue the academic opportunities (incl. extra-curricular events, which come often)
Travel and explore the city often.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: None that come to mind.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Generally just experiencing the local lifestyle more than you would on a vacation.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Pushing through some difficult courses and preparing for exams, which can be intense.

questions.question: Any other comments?

questions.answer: Yes
